prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1486; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a collision in which the insured vehicle was struck while turning left at an intersection. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the statements from the other driver and two independent witnesses, who all describe the collision in the same way as the claimant. Scene photographs were obtained and are consistent with the reported sequence of events.

Entry 3: Police report confirms the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact. The driver is listed as a named operator on the policy, and no coverage concerns have been identified.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection completed. Most of the damage lines up with the impact described, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior records or the repair history reviewed so far.

Entry 5: Medical records show a wrist fracture, which fits the type and force of a collision of this kind. Treatment followed a typical course and tapered off as the claimant's condition improved. Records also show treatment to the same body area within the past two years, and that prior condition is adding to the current complaints.

Entry 6: Claimant has given the same account of the accident in each conversation to date, with no changes in the details. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 7: File reviewed and considered ready for the next stage of evaluation. Counsel to be advised of the current findings, and the medical and repair documentation will be requested in full.
